tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear Path for Target Disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a disk that is not on top, first relocate every smaller disk that sits above it to other pegs so the target disk becomes the topmost disk before moving it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a disk that has smaller disks stacked above it on its source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If peg A has [4,2,1] (top 1) and you need to move disk 4, first move disks 1 and 2 elsewhere, then move disk 4.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Build Goal Stack in Decreasing Size
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Construct the final tower on the goal peg by placing disks from the largest down to the smallest, never putting a larger disk on a smaller one, so each newly placed disk becomes the new top of the goal stack.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When assembling the final configuration on the target peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To achieve [5,4,3,2,1] on peg C, first move disk 5, then disk 4, then disk 3, and so on.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Phase Planning (Move‑k‑Disks)
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Solve the sub‑problem of moving k disks by recursively moving the top k‑1 disks to an auxiliary peg, moving the k‑th (largest) disk to the target peg, then moving the k‑1 disks from the auxiliary onto the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to transfer a stack of several disks between pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move three disks from A to C using B: move two disks A→B, move disk 3 A→C, then move two disks B→C.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Do Not Prematurely Place Small Disks on Goal
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never move a small disk onto the goal peg before all larger disks that must sit below it have already been placed in their final positions; otherwise the small disk will have to be moved again.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During construction of the goal stack, especially when the goal peg already contains some disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Do not place disk 1 on the goal peg before disks 5, 4, 3, 2 are already stacked there.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Legal Move Invariant
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Every move must satisfy two conditions: the source disk is the topmost disk on its peg, and the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: For each individual move you generate.
tower-of-hanoi.example: You cannot move disk 3 onto a peg whose top disk is disk 2 because 3 > 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat Existing Goal Disks as Fixed Base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Once a disk is correctly placed on the goal peg and all larger disks beneath it are also correctly placed, treat that disk as immovable; never move it again.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After a disk has reached its final position in the goal stack.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After placing disk 5 at the bottom of the goal peg, never move disk 5 again.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Exploit the Smallest Disk’s Flexibility
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without violating size constraints, making it an ideal temporary buffer to enable moves of larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need a free peg or a temporary placeholder while preserving legality.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Move disk 1 to an empty peg to free up a peg for moving disk 4.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Post‑Construction Verification
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the complete move list, replay the moves from the initial configuration to verify that each move is legal and that the final configuration matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: As a final sanity check before outputting the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Simulate the sequence step‑by‑step and compare the resulting configuration with the target stack.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recognize Classic Single‑Peg Configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Detect when all disks start stacked on a single peg and the goal is the same ordered stack on another peg; in this case you can apply the standard Hanoi solution directly (2ⁿ‑1 moves).
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the initial state consists of one full tower on one peg and the goal is a full tower on a different peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Start with all disks on peg 0, goal all on peg 2 → use the classic recursive algorithm.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Generate Moves Recursively with Explicit Disk IDs
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Implement the recursive Hanoi algorithm by explicitly naming the disk being moved in each step, rather than using generic move commands; this avoids ambiguity and ensures correct ordering.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When programmatically constructing the move list for a Hanoi problem.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Output [3, 0, 2] to indicate moving disk 3 from peg 0 to peg 2.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Violating size rule: moving a larger disk onto a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may focus on moving the desired disk without checking the size of the destination's top disk.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always compare the moving disk's size with the destination peg's top disk; only move if the destination is empty or its top disk is larger.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk without clearing the path.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model sometimes assumes a disk can be lifted directly, ignoring the rule that only the topmost disk may be moved.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before moving any disk, verify it is the topmost disk on its peg; if not, first move all smaller disks above it elsewhere.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Final configuration does not match the goal state.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The generated move sequence may stop prematurely or misplace a disk, leading to a mismatched end state.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: After generating the move list, replay it from the initial configuration and compare the resulting arrangement with the goal; adjust moves if they differ.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Incorrect peg indexing (off‑by‑one or swapped pegs).
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Confusion between 0‑based indexing used by the verifier and natural 1‑based or named peg references.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Consistently use 0‑based peg numbers throughout reasoning and when writing moves; double‑check each move's source and destination indices.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Premature placement of small disks on the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may move a small disk to the goal peg early, forgetting that larger disks still need to be placed beneath it.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Only place a small disk on the goal peg after all larger disks that belong below it have already been fixed in their final positions.
